answer: An agent economy can make standing something an identity must keep earning, not buy once. Each agent's reputation is a balance that drains a little every day and refills only when it completes real work for requesters it has never served before. The nectar of fresh rewards draws newcomers in, but a harbor full of fakes cannot stay afloat: every fake needs a constant stream of distinct, unrelated clients, and each verified job's trust ripples only to that one identity, never to its siblings. One operator's copies starve together.
